description: Single-panel table image (no plot, micrograph or schematic). The caption titles it "Volume fraction and mean radius of (Ti, V)C and κ". Column headers are "Samples", "(Ti, V) C" and "κ"; each of the four sample labels occupies two sub-rows whose left-hand descriptors are "Volume fraction (%)" and "Mean radius (nm)". The tabulated alloys are M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS and M2-30. M1-SS shows a dash in every measurement cell, i.e. neither (Ti, V)C nor κ-carbide was quantified. M1-30 has no (Ti, V)C but κ-carbide with a volume fraction of 7.4 ± 3.4 % and a mean radius of 10.8 ± 6.2 nm. M2-SS contains (Ti, V)C at 2.4 ± 1.4 % and 35.8 ± 20.1 nm, with no κ reported. M2-30 is the only condition containing both phases: (Ti, V)C at 2.3 ± 1.7 % with 37.1 ± 22.6 nm, plus κ-carbide at 3.2 ± 2.8 % with 9.7 ± 8.5 nm. All entries are mean ± standard deviation; only units %, nm and dashes are printed, and no graph or error-bar panel accompanies the table. The table demonstrates that Ti and V addition produces coarse (Ti, V)C particles while markedly reducing both the volume fraction and the mean radius of κ-carbide after aging.

observations.observation: The image is a single table with the column headers 'Samples', '(Ti, V) C' and 'κ'.
Each sample block contains two sub-rows labelled 'Volume fraction (%)' and 'Mean radius (nm)'.
Four sample labels are tabulated: M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS and M2-30.
For M1-SS every cell of both the (Ti, V) C and κ columns contains a dash, indicating no value reported.
M1-30 reports κ-carbide volume fraction 7.4 ± 3.4 % and mean radius 10.8 ± 6.2 nm, with dashes in the (Ti, V) C column.
M2-SS reports (Ti, V) C volume fraction 2.4 ± 1.4 % and mean radius 35.8 ± 20.1 nm, with dashes in the κ column.
M2-30 reports (Ti, V) C volume fraction 2.3 ± 1.7 % and mean radius 37.1 ± 22.6 nm.
M2-30 reports κ-carbide volume fraction 3.2 ± 2.8 % and mean radius 9.7 ± 8.5 nm, making it the only condition with both precipitates quantified.
Every numeric entry in the table is given as a mean with a ± standard deviation; the only units printed are % and nm.
The caption states the table reports the volume fraction and mean radius of (Ti, V)C and κ.

The abstract states that without Ti and V addition κ-carbides precipitate uniformly after aging with an average size of 10.8 ± 6.2 nm and a volume fraction of 7.4, matching the M1-30 row of the table.
